prompt:
Scene:
A square-format vertical-subject photograph of a chrome pool ladder descending into an empty deep end, shot with 90s direct flash at night. The room is a community recreation pool with high painted ceiling. Only the flash lights the ladder; beyond the ladder, the deep-end basin falls into soft darkness. 35mm film grain and a slight green-yellow cast.

Subject:
A four-rung stainless steel pool ladder bolted to the deck with two anchor plates, rungs curving into the basin. The basin bottom beneath the ladder is dry concrete with faded navy depth markings stenciled nearby. Wall tile near the ladder is cobalt blue at the waterline and pale ivory above. One spent rubber cap lies on the deck beside a drain grate.

Important details:
The ladder must catch the flash cleanly with hot specular highlights on polished chrome. The drop below the last rung must read as deeper than the near deck, implying this is the deep end. Faint condensation should be visible on the tile. The feeling is 'ladder waiting for a swimmer who never returns'. No person, no splash, no water.

Use case:
Empty Pool single study 2/5, close study of a deep-end ladder.

Constraints:
No readable text (depth number is only partially legible as stencil strokes), no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no person, no reflection of photographer in chrome, no cinematic lens flare.
